objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on TOUCH-CENSUS-20261118-001's direction 2 (after RING-GROWTH-20261118-001): in all 147 census exceptions to the chain rule the dimension was the largest class of chains born together plus one. Freeze a corrected rule (classes whose partners share a neighbour are linked; the dimension is the largest sum of class sizes over a linked component), score it on every growing arrangement of the census with a birth and on a sample of six-knot arrangements. Stop at a rule that predicts every case, or a counterexample. Serves G17.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Partially successful; referee pending): chains of offshoots born in one round whose partners share a neighbour add their dimensions under the cheapest counts; the linked-class rule matches 11,649 of 11,658 census arrangements with a birth and 148 of 149 six-knot ones, never overshooting; ten combine through a link not yet found (two round-1 births from start knots sharing a distinction; the naive repair overshoots 889).
stop_rule: One frozen computation, read-out, referee hand-off, report.
title: When do separately born chains combine?
